task.title: Style a formula
task.shortdesc: You style a formula with attributes of the MathML elements, with CSS rules for the elements, and with three properties that CSS adds for math: math-style, math-depth and math-shift.

info.p: These attributes of MathML elements set a style for the element and for what it holds. mstyle exists to hold them for a group of elements, and an attribute on an element wins over the same attribute on an mstyle around it:

ul.li: mathcolor sets the color of the text, and mathbackground the color behind it.
mathsize sets the size of the text: a length, a percentage, or one of small, normal and big.

mathvariant chooses a style of letters for a token. normal is upright, and the others are bold, italic, bold-italic, double-struck, script, bold-script, fraktur, bold-fraktur, sans-serif, bold-sans-serif, sans-serif-italic, sans-serif-bold-italic and monospace. Four more values, initial, tailed, looped and stretched, choose the forms of Arabic letters.
dir is ltr or rtl. An rtl formula runs from right to left, and its fences are mirrored.

info.p: The merror element has a red border and a light yellow background, to show an error.

The elements of a formula are elements of your document, so the rules of your style sheet reach them. Select them with the MathML namespace, and with the class and style attributes that MathML elements can have. A rule of your style sheet wins over the attributes of the previous step. The style attribute wins over a rule:

A formula is a row of boxes, and the box properties work on them. A border, a padding and a margin on an element are kept around its content, and the other elements of the formula are spaced around the result. float has no effect on the elements of a formula. In a formula from a file, the rules are those of its own style sheet.
The properties content, counter-reset, counter-increment and counter-set work on the elements of a formula, and so do ::before and ::after. A rule can add text before and after an element:

The generated text is a box of its own, among the children of the element. Generate it on an mi, an mn, an mo, an mtext, an mrow, an mtd or the math element. An element with a fixed number of children, such as mfrac or msup, that gets one more child is laid out as a row of its children.

Counters give an equation a number. Put an empty cell at the end of each row of equations, count with counter-increment and show the number in ::before. The counters of your document run through its formulas in document order, so the first equation of the second formula has the number that follows the last equation of the first. A formula file has counters of its own, which start at 0:

info.p: A script, a limit or an index is smaller than the text it belongs to. The script level of an element says how many such steps it is down from the text: the text has level 0, a superscript has level 1, and a script of a script has level 2. Each level is smaller than the one before. The font gives the sizes of the first two levels in its MATH table, and a level after them is 71% of the level before it. CSSMedia does not make the text smaller than 8pt.
Set the level of an element with scriptlevel, and give the size of its text with mathsize:
A value such as 2 sets the level. A value with a sign, such as +1 or -1, adds to the level of the parent.
The attributes scriptsizemultiplier and scriptminsize of mstyle set the factor for each level and the least size, in place of the values of the font and the 8pt above.
CSS has three properties for math. They are inherited, and the attributes above set them:

ul.li: math-depth is the script level. It takes an integer, add(an integer), or auto-add, which adds one level in a compact style and none in a normal style. The attribute scriptlevel sets it. The rule m|mi { math-depth: 2; } makes every identifier of level 2.

math-style is normal for display style, with the full size of fractions and limits, and compact for a style that saves room. The attribute displaystyle of mstyle sets it: true is normal, and false is compact. A math element with display="block" is normal, and the other ones are compact.
math-shift is normal or compact. In compact, the superscripts of the element are raised less, so that they do not collide with the line above, as under a root bar or in a denominator.

info.p: Three more values of CSS properties exist for math. The values block math and inline math of display make an element a formula that is block or inline, and the value math of font-size gives the size that the script level calls for. The value math-auto of text-transform turns one letter into its italic form. CSSMedia sets all three in the rules it has for MathML elements, so you seldom write them.
